stories.title: Australian police arrest two men accused of widespread open-source software hacking
stories.summary: Australian police will charge two men over hacking open-source software used by thousands of businesses worldwide. The hackers inserted malicious code that stole over 500,000 credentials and 300 gigabytes of data, affecting more than 1,000 organisations globally. The investigation involved the FBI and cybersecurity firms, highlighting TeamPCP as a major cyber threat in 2026, described as a skilled collective rather than a unified group. The Australian police announced charges on Aug 27 against two men accused of participating in a cybercrime syndicate that targeted widely used open-source software to compromise thousands of global businesses. The Australian men face a combined 14 charges for their alleged roles in TeamPCP, a hacking collective that inserted malicious code into popular tools to compromise businesses, according to a statement from the Australian Federal. Police. Some of the businesses were later extorted, according to a July Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) advisory. The police did not name the men, but the Australian Broadcasting Corporation identified them as Ruben Ian Thomson, 21, and Louis Michael Gaebler, 23. Nick Scerri, a lawyer for Thomson, did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside of normal business hours. Reuters could not immediately find an attorney for Gaebler. The malicious code potentially compromised more than 1,000 organisations globally, enabling the theft of more than 500,000 credentials and more than 300 gigabytes of data, according to the police. The police said they conducted a parallel investigation into the men with the FBI starting in April after receiving information from multiple unnamed cybersecurity threat assessment companies.

stories.title: Iran could harm US economic interests in response to sanctions — security official
stories.summary: CAIRO, August 28. Iran could jeopardize US economic interests in the Middle East if Washington mounts its pressure of sanctions, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei said. "In the event of intensified US economic pressure on Iran, we will respond with countermeasures that will affect US interests in the region, " he told Lebanon’s Al Manar television channel without specifying the nature of these measures. Rezaei added that, in his opinion, Washington’s shift toward economic pressure demonstrates that "a military solution to the conflict produces limited results." The Axios portal reported on August 26 that Washington was not planning new attacks on Iran any time soon as it will focus on other means of pressure on Tehran, including sanctions.
